proof_architecture: Terminal reduction starts from exact scalar identities of the prior subdivision. Rational diagonal primitives separate resonant and nonresonant monomials using a fixed denominator lattice. Nozero boxes use integrated displacement; simple roots are analytically linearized; annular power/log changes and resonance redoing reduce transfers to ordinary analytic, additive, regular one-rate or mixed packet models.

Every kernel is defined on independent-argument neighborhoods and matched to actual flow on a regular endpoint graph, including independently proposed mismatched endpoints. Corrected right amplitudes cancel the proposed final state before imposing matching. Exact open identities, implicit derivatives and triangular finite state/jet graphs retain every chain-rule term. Internal subdivisions use one fixed finite K after a sequence regime is chosen and are not new geometric passage types.

Boundary analysis separates positive-margin completeness from vanishing-margin extension. Three nested boxes and integrated forcing give state room on admitted closures. Bounded normalized ratios/root graphs extend analytically after divisor clearing, with graph Jacobians required nonzero only at the sequence points; any divergent recoverable auxiliary coordinate instead enters the packet flag analysis.

The projection principle assumes absolute isolated-zero finiteness for every finite differential/algebraic closure system, including added coordinates and specialized parameters. Proper barriers 1+|p|²+|x|²+Σg_j⁻², generic Morse tilts, multiplier equations, Sard/Fubini and induction on parameter dimension convert that hereditary zero property into uniform fiber component counts on full-row-rank charts.

Finite geometric words produce matching systems with physical endpoints shared by links, one scalar transfer equation per link, regular auxiliary ties and explicit strict margins. At a hyperbolic cycle the transverse cyclic Jacobian has rows dr_(j+1)−h_jdr_j and is invertible because Πh_j≠1; tangential cut positions account for the free dimensions. Analytic continuation shows one regular fiber component cannot contain representations of two different cycles. Absolute zero finiteness for the full closure is then obtained by a bounded analytic-limit alternative or a divergent retestable packet-flag alternative, using earlier primitive/absolute-zero theorems.

Sum finitely many component bounds over words and maximal-minor charts and add finite boundary exceptions. For a finite collection of possibly nonhyperbolic cycles, rotate V to V+μJV; the transverse parameter derivative satisfies a positive-forcing determinant equation. One common sign yields at least the original total number of hyperbolic cycles, counting two from favored even-order cycles. Affine spatial scaling puts any finite collection into the fixed square; exceeding the uniform bound would give a finite countercollection.
